items: Regulate Yourself First: Take a deep breath and check your own emotional state before responding so you can stay calm and regulated during your toddler's tantrum.
Regulate Yourself First: Remind yourself that tantrums are a normal developmental behavior and not a reflection of your parenting ability or your child's character.
Regulate Yourself First: Stay physically present with your toddler during the tantrum without trying to immediately stop or fix their emotional outburst.
Regulate Yourself First: Model calm breathing and emotional regulation for your toddler so they learn to manage big feelings by watching you stay steady.
Respond With CORE: Validate your child's feelings with simple words like 'I see you're really upset' without trying to solve the problem while they're at peak intensity.
Respond With CORE: Avoid reasoning, giving in to demands, unnecessary physical restraint, or shaming your child during the peak of a tantrum.
Respond With CORE: Offer gentle regulation support by suggesting deep breaths or modeling slow breathing while staying nearby and calm for your child.
Respond With CORE: Give your toddler empty space and time for the tantrum to naturally subside without rushing to stop it or fill the silence.
After Care and Red Flags: Once everyone is calm, talk with your toddler about what happened using simple words to help them name their feelings and build emotional vocabulary.
After Care and Red Flags: Reconnect with your child through comfort and warmth after the tantrum ends before moving back to regular activities or discipline.
After Care and Red Flags: Consult your pediatrician if tantrums last more than 15 minutes regularly, cause injury, or your child appears glassy-eyed and disconnected.
After Care and Red Flags: Identify one trigger situation this week and practice the CORE method before the next tantrum hits so you're prepared.
